text: The one sided limit is wrong and every point depending on it is lost. When you evaluate a one sided limit at a boundary, you must use the branch that applies on that side of the boundary. Just to the left of x = 1, the function rule is 2x + 3, which gives a left-hand limit of 5. Just to the right of x = 1 and at x = 1 itself, the rule is kx - 1, which gives both the right-hand limit and the function value as k - 1. For the function to be continuous at x = 1, these one sided limits must be equal.
